findings.issue_text: [BUG] The 'menu contains exactly 4 items' assertion conflicts with the permissions granted in beforeEach: with AlertingRuleDelete and folder delete access granted, AlertRuleMenu also renders Delete (and Pause, since update is granted), so byRole('menuitem').getAll() returns more than 4 and expect(menuItems.length).toBe(4) fails. CI fails on this new test; the count assertion cannot pass while beforeEach grants delete/update permissions, so the PR cannot merge as written.

[ADVISORY] A bespoke `skipToken` Symbol is exported from useAbilities.ts even though the codebase (RTK Query / @tanstack/react-query based hooks) already has a skipToken concept, creating two parallel 'skip' conventions for the same pattern. The next contributor wiring pause/restore or another hook will import one symbol where the other is expected (or re-invent a third), and a mismatch silently degrades to `undefined` rule rather than an explicit skip, making future list-view hooks harder to reason about.

[ADVISORY] AlertRuleMenu unconditionally runs both useRulerRuleAbilities and useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities, and the 'skip' path still executes useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities (useFolder, useGrafanaRulesSilenceSupport, useCanSilenceInFolder) — so every rule row in the list, including datasource (Mimir) rules that can never be Grafana-managed, fires the folder/silence-support query machinery. On the ~80-rule list page the diff multiplies per-row hook work (folder lookups and silence-support checks that were previously ruler-API-guarded), degrading list performance for users with many datasource rules.

[ADVISORY] useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities contains the stray marker comment `// duplicate` on the useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable call line, indicating unfinished copy-paste rather than documentation. Future readers cannot tell whether 'duplicate' refers to duplicated rules, a duplicated hook, or leftover TODO text, slowing comprehension of the permission-check path that governs edit/delete buttons.

[ADVISORY] RuleActionsButtons.V2 silently returns null when getEditableIdentifier cannot build an identifier (non-Grafana promRule with no rulerRule), while logging only a warning — the entire action row (including Delete/View-only affordances that do not need an edit identifier) disappears. A user browsing a list containing a non-Grafana promRule that reaches this component gets a rule row with no actions at all and only a backend analytics warning; the early return conflates 'cannot edit' with 'cannot render any button'.

[BUG] useAllRulerRuleAbilities hard-codes isFederated = false with a TODO, dropping the isFederatedRuleGroup immutability check that the previous useAllAlertRuleAbilities performed. Mimir federated rule groups, which were previously immutable (edit/delete/delete-permanently shown as NotSupported via immutableRule), now render Edit and Delete as supported/allowed, so a user with permissions can trigger edit/delete flows against federated rules the old code refused; the deprecated wrapper useAllAlertRuleAbilities delegates to this function, so the rule-details and list views both lose the federated guard.

[BUG] GrafanaGroupLoader drops the ruler-API comparison entirely, so the Creating state (ruler-only rules) and Deleting state (prom-only rules) list items are no longer rendered. A user who just created a Grafana rule sees it disappear from the list until Prometheus propagation completes (previously shown with a 'Creating' icon), and a just-deleted rule lingers with no 'Deleting' indicator — the diff also deletes the two tests that covered these states ('should render rule with url and creating state when only ruler rule exists', 'should render delete rule operation list item when only prom rule exists') instead of porting them, leaving the regression unverified.

[BUG] The new GrafanaRuleListItem builds the view URL without the returnTo parameter that the deleted GrafanaRuleLoader consistently attached via createReturnTo(). Users clicking a rule from the list view land on the rule-view page without the 'return to list' context, losing the back-navigation behavior the previous list entry provided on every entry point (both FilterView and GrafanaGroupLoader now route through this component).

[ADVISORY] No test in the diff exercises the new OR-fallback semantics in AlertRuleMenu (an action enabled via grafanaPromRuleAbility while the ruler ability denies it, or vice versa). The RBAC regression risk is the entire point of this diff, yet RulesTable.test.tsx only mocks one branch at a time (each test sets the plural hooks to deny-all defaults or grant-all), so a wiring mistake — e.g. ANDing instead of ORing, or reading grafanaDeleteAllowed as grafanaDeleteSupported — would pass the full suite; a future regression in permission gating for the alert list view ships undetected.

[ADVISORY] The Silence ability in useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities is [silenceSupported, canSilenceInFolder && isAlertingRule], replacing useCanSilence without a test verifying the permission semantics survived the rewrite. The old ruler path's useCanSilence encapsulated datasource/silence RBAC checks; if useCanSilenceInFolder does not include the AlertingSilenceCreate permission check for the folder metadata, users without silence-create permission see an enabled Silence menu item in the new list view; the new GrafanaGroupLoader menu test only asserts the happy path (all permissions granted, 4 items visible) and never asserts silence is hidden when AlertingSilenceCreate is denied.

[BUG] Removing the ruler API from GrafanaGroupLoader silently deletes the previously rendered 'Creating' and 'Deleting' intermediate rule states, which is not traceable to the stated intent of switching ability checks to promRule. Users who just created a rule see nothing in the list until Prometheus propagation completes, and users who just deleted a rule see a stale 'Deleting'-state row vanish with no feedback; the old code explicitly rendered RuleOperationListItem/Creating rows for exactly this gap.

[BUG] useAllAlertRuleAbilities re-implementation hardcodes isFederated = false with a TODO, dropping federated-rule-group immutability enforcement that the deprecated implementation enforced via isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group). For federated Grafana rule groups, the Edit/Delete buttons now render as supported-and-allowed where they were previously forced to NotSupported, letting users attempt edits/deletes of federated rules that the backend rejects or corrupts.

[ADVISORY] The new GrafanaRuleListItem drops the returnTo query parameter from the rule view href that the deleted GrafanaRuleLoader's GrafanaRuleListItem always appended. Users navigating from the rule list into a rule view and then editing lose their list filter/pagination context on return, a regression invisible to the stated 'switch to promRule' intent.

[ADVISORY] The line 'const { isEditable, isRemovable, loading } = useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable(rule); // duplicate' leaves a stray 'duplicate' comment in shipped code, suggesting an unresolved copy-paste concern about the hook itself. The next maintainer cannot tell whether 'duplicate' flags a real correctness concern or dead note, making any change to this hook riskier to review.

[ADVISORY] The PR modifies RuleDetails.test.tsx (rewiring the cloud rule mock to a mimir datasource) even though nothing in the stated intent — list-view ruler-API removal and promRule abilities — touches RuleDetails, indicating hidden coupling where these hook refactors break unrelated tests. The test churn reveals that useAllRulerRuleAbilities' signature/behavior change rippled into components outside the alert list view; any future maintainer of RuleDetails must now understand this PR's datasource plumbing to keep the test green.

[BUG] Removing the Ruler API fetch and rendering only Prometheus rules drops newly created rules from the list until Prometheus propagation completes, deleting the Creating/Deleting transitional states the previous code explicitly handled. A user who creates or deletes a Grafana-managed rule sees it vanish from the rule list (no 'Creating' placeholder) or sees a deleted rule remain with no 'Deleting' indicator until the Prometheus rule API catches up; the diff even deletes the tests that asserted this behavior instead of updating them.

[BUG] useAllAlertRuleAbilities now hardcodes isFederated = false (with a TODO) because the refactor to useAllRulerRuleAbilities(rule, groupIdentifier) dropped the CombinedRule, so federated rule groups are no longer recognized as immutable. Every existing caller of useAllAlertRuleAbilities — which served the ~80-rule list page — now marks federated Mimir rules as editable/removable, letting users attempt edit/delete operations on federated rules that the backend will reject or that were previously correctly disabled; this is a silent behavioral regression shipped to all existing call sites, not just the refactored list view.

[BUG] AlertRuleMenu unconditionally calls useRulerRuleAbilities(rulerRule, groupIdentifier, ...) and ORs the result with Grafana prom-rule abilities, so when rulerRule is undefined the ruler hook's loading/unsupported result is not distinguished from a definitive 'not allowed', and for non-Grafana datasource prom rules passed as promRule both paths can misreport support. On the new list view (rulerRule undefined), while the folder/permission queries load, canPause/canDelete/etc. compute from a ruler path that reports [false,false] or [undefined,undefined] and OR-ing with an equally-loading grafana path yields flickering menus where actions appear/disappear across renders; for cloud (Mimir) rules the grafana path receives skipToken so menu items depend solely on a ruler rule the list view no longer fetches.

[ADVISORY] The rewritten GrafanaRuleListItem drops the createReturnTo() query parameter from the rule href that the deleted GrafanaRuleLoader version attached (href: createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`, { returnTo })). Users clicking a rule from the list view, then navigating back from the rule details/edit page, lose their list filters and scroll position because the returnTo context is no longer propagated; every list-view entry point regresses this UX.

[ADVISORY] isPaused is now taken solely from rule?.isPaused with no rulerRule fallback, unlike the previous version's isPaused: rule?.isPaused ?? is_paused. Any consumer rendering a GrafanaRuleListItem whose prom rule payload lacks isPaused (or where the field is undefined mid-poll) shows the rule as not-paused when it is, displaying wrong state in the list; minor because prom rules normally carry the flag, but the deletion test removal makes this path untested.

[ADVISORY] getEditableIdentifier returns undefined and the component returns null for any promRule that is not a Grafana prom rule (e.g. a cloud Mimir prom rule reaching this path after the ruler API was removed from the list view), silently rendering no action buttons at all. If a datasource-backed prom rule flows into RuleActionsButtons.V2 (the RequireAtLeastOne type permits promRule-only), the user gets zero actions with only an analytics logWarning — no edit/delete affordance and no error surfaced; the guard converts a contract violation into an invisible feature loss.

[ADVISORY] useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable returns loading from useFolder, but when folder resolves it returns loading=false with isEditable/isRemovable computed — yet while the folder request is in flight it returns loading:true with isEditable:false, and callers like useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities map MaybeSupported = loading ? NotSupported : AlwaysSupported, so during load all actions read as NotSupported with no distinct loading signal exported. Components OR-ing these abilities (AlertRuleMenu) cannot distinguish 'still loading' from 'definitively denied', causing menu items to pop in after a folder-permission round trip per rule — multiplied by ~80 rules on the list page this is also a per-rule useFolder fetch pattern (N requests for N rules in one group's folder, same folderUid) that has no batching.

[BUG] useAllRulerRuleAbilities silently hardcodes `const isFederated = false;` behind a TODO, dropping the federated-rule-group immutability check that the previous implementation (via useAllAlertRuleAbilities and isFederatedRuleGroup) enforced. Federated Grafana rule groups are now reported as editable/removable/duplicable, so users on instances with federated groups see and can act on Edit/Delete/Pause menu entries the previous RBAC logic correctly suppressed; the immutableRule gate that protected them is gone with no feature flag or migration note.

[BUG] The rewritten GrafanaRuleListItem builds the rule href as `createRelativeUrl(\`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view\`)`, dropping the `createReturnTo()` query parameter that the deleted GrafanaRuleLoader.tsx version always appended (`createRelativeUrl(..., { returnTo })`). Users who navigate from the alert list into a rule and then click Back/return links lose their list context (filters, scroll, pagination) because the view page no longer knows where to return; this UX contract changed silently as a side effect of the loader refactor.

[ADVISORY] The refactor deletes both transient-state behaviors of the group list: rules present only in the ruler API (RuleOperation.Creating) and rules present only in Prometheus (RuleOperation.Deleting, rendered via RuleOperationListItem) are no longer rendered at all, and the corresponding tests ('should render rule with url and creating state when only ruler rule exists', 'should render delete rule operation list item when only prom rule exists') were removed rather than ported. During rule creation/deletion propagation windows, rules flicker in and out of the list instead of showing Creating/Deleting placeholders, and deleting coverage for the deleted behavior means a future regression to transient-state handling would pass CI; the intent change (strong-consistency assumption) is plausible but is not stated as accepted anywhere in the diff and is enforced by deleting the tests that documented the old contract.

[ADVISORY] AlertRuleMenu now ORs ruler-based and prom-based abilities (e.g. `canPause = (pauseSupported && pauseAllowed) || (grafanaPauseSupported && grafanaPauseAllowed)`), so any single source granting an ability wins even when the other source explicitly denies it. When a rule is rendered with both a rulerRule and a promRule whose ability computations disagree (e.g. folder permissions checked via useFolder say deny while the ruler path says allow, or vice versa), the menu shows actions the denying source forbids — the previous behavior granted an action only when the (single) ruler check allowed it; this broadening of the permission gate shipped with no test asserting the OR semantics for the disagreeing case.

[ADVISORY] RuleActionsButtons now returns null whenever getEditableIdentifier cannot construct an identifier (rule undefined and promRule not a Grafana rule), with only a logWarning, replacing the previous contract where the component always rendered buttons for its required RulerRuleDTO input. A caller passing a non-Grafana promRule (or a datasource rule shape) gets a silently empty actions column with no user-visible error or fallback View button, and existing call sites that previously relied on always getting a rendered component now render nothing for rule types the new identifier logic doesn't recognize.

[ADVISORY] The new Grafana-prom-rule ability path replaces useCanSilence (which checked alertmanager selection/permissions) with useCanSilenceInFolder + useGrafanaRulesSilenceSupport, a different and potentially weaker derivation for the Silence action. Users in a setup where they hold AlertingSilenceCreate on the folder but lack the alertmanager-level silence permission the old path enforced will see an enabled Silence menu item / drawer that fails on submit — a visible authorization-check drift between the ruler path and the prom-rule path; frontend-only (server still enforces), but the two code paths now make contradictory authorization claims for the same action.

[ADVISORY] canPause/canDelete/canDuplicate/canSilence/canExport are computed as a logical OR of the ruler-rule ability and the Grafana-prom-rule ability, so one path granting suffices even when the other path explicitly denies (e.g. immutable/provisioned rules). A provisioned rule marked NotSupported by the ruler path will still surface menu actions if the prom-rule path (useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities, which computes isProvisioned from the prom DTO's provenance field) resolves differently — e.g. when rulerRule and promRule provenance data diverge during propagation lag, the menu shows destructive actions (Delete, Pause) on a provisioned rule; server-side enforcement catches the mutation, but users get confusing failed operations and the UI's immutability guarantee is inconsistent across the two parallel permission derivations.

[ADVISORY] The new OR-composition of ruler and grafana prom abilities (canPause/canDelete/canDuplicate/canSilence/canExport = rulerAbility || grafanaAbility) has no test that verifies it, because RulesTable.test.tsx jest.mock's the entire useAbilities module and both mocks return identical values for the same action. Changing `||` to `&&`, or dropping the grafana prom branch entirely, passes every test in this diff — e.g. a Grafana rule whose ruler ability is [false,false] but grafana prom ability is [true,true] would silently lose its Delete/Duplicate menu items in production while the suite stays green; users on the alert list view get bitten the next time this composition is edited.

[ADVISORY] The new hook useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities (~65 lines of behavior-bearing logic: skipToken/undefined-rule path, isProvisionedPromRule gating, silenceSupported/canSilenceInFolder, isAlertingRule gating of Silence/Export/Pause/DeletePermanently) has zero direct test coverage in this diff. I checked the test files in the diff (RuleDetails.test.tsx, RulesTable.test.tsx, GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx): RulesTable mocks the whole module, RuleDetails only changes a fixture's rulesSource, and GrafanaGroupLoader.test only asserts edit-button presence and menu-item presence for a fully-permissioned alerting rule — a regression in e.g. `[AlertRuleAction.Silence]: [silenceSupported, canSilenceInFolder && isAlertingRule]` (recording rules gaining a Silence menu item, or alerting rules losing it when folderUid resolves late during `loading`) ships undetected.

[ADVISORY] The menu-content test ends with a bare count assertion `expect(menuItems.length).toBe(4)` while the `ui.menuItems.delete()` selector it defines is never asserted, so Delete's presence/absence is never verified despite delete permissions being granted in beforeEach. The assertion verifies a count, not content: a regression that swaps one menu item for another (e.g. Delete failing to render, or an unexpected Pause item appearing, keeping the count at 4) passes the test; the very action (Delete) the beforeEach explicitly grants via setFolderAccessControl is the one never checked, giving false confidence that the permission wiring in the new prom-rule path works.

[ADVISORY] The 'should render More button with action menu options' test only asserts `toBeInTheDocument()`, `toHaveAttribute('aria-label', 'More')` and `toHaveTextContent('More')` — assertions that pass regardless of whether any ability/permission logic in AlertRuleMenu or RuleActionsButtons is correct. This test provides false confidence while replacing the deleted creating-state/deleting-state tests: it would pass even if the component rendered the More button but every menu action was wrongly gated off (or wrongly gated on), so the refactored permission path it nominally covers is exercised without being verified.

[ADVISORY] The new GrafanaRuleListItem component has three rendering branches (alerting / recording / unknown) but no test in this diff renders a recording rule or an unknown-type rule through it — GrafanaGroupLoader.test only ever renders alerting rules. I checked RuleDetails.test.tsx, RulesTable.test.tsx and GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx; none constructs a recording or unknown-typed GrafanaPromRuleDTO, so a regression in the RecordingRuleListItem branch (e.g. showLocation no longer forwarded, which silently changed semantics vs the deleted GrafanaRuleLoader that passed showLocation via commonProps) ships undetected; recording-rule users see wrong list items.

[ADVISORY] The new early-return path `if (!identifier) { return null; }` (including the logWarning branch in getEditableIdentifier when a non-grafana promRule arrives with no ruler rule) and the new promRule branch of getIsProvisioned are never triggered by any test in the diff. RulesTable.test.tsx mocks all ability hooks and always supplies ruler-backed rules, so the silently-renders-nothing failure mode (a datasource-type promRule passed to the new list item silently losing all action buttons with only a warning log) is unexercised — a regression that makes the component return null for a wider class of rules than intended would pass the suite.

[ADVISORY] The permission-denied test asserts only that the Edit button disappears and the More button remains, but never opens the menu to assert which actions are hidden for a user without update/delete permissions. The comment claims the More button remains 'for other actions like viewing', but nothing verifies the menu contents under denied permissions — e.g. if the new OR-composition in AlertRuleMenu lets Duplicate or Delete through via the ruler-ability branch (which runs with an undefined rulerRule in the new prom-only list item), users without delete permission would see actionable Delete/Duplicate items in production while this test stays green.

[BUG] The rewrite drops ruler-only rules (state Creating) and prom-only rules (state Deleting) from the list entirely, because rendering now maps only over promResponse.data.groups.at(0)?.rules. A rule just created via the ruler API but not yet propagated to Prometheus disappears from the list with no Creating indicator, and a just-deleted rule shows a stale Deleting entry gone; users see inconsistent rule inventories during propagation windows and previously-surfaced RuleOperationListItem states are silently lost.

[BUG] useRulerRuleAbility (the singular hook) is invoked with a now-optional `rule` that is undefined when the component is used from the prom-rule-only list path, but this diff widened only the plural useRulerRuleAbilities to accept undefined — the singular hook's contract still requires RulerRuleDTO. When GrafanaRuleListItem renders RuleActionsButtons with only promRule, the singular hook receives undefined and either fails to compile or issues a ruler-API ability evaluation against an undefined rule, breaking the edit-button gating on the new list view.

[ADVISORY] The new GrafanaRuleListItem drops the `returnTo` query parameter that the deleted GrafanaRuleLoader added via createReturnTo(), and drops the `is_paused` fallback from the ruler rule (isPaused: rule?.isPaused with no ruler fallback). Users who click a rule in the list and then Edit/View lose the return-to-list navigation they previously had, and during creation/propagation windows a brand-new paused rule shows an unpaused indicator because the prom payload hasn't caught up with ruler's is_paused.

[ADVISORY] summary is now sourced from rule.annotations?.summary (prom payload) instead of the ruler rule's annotations, and the entire item no longer merges ruler-rule data, so fields absent from GrafanaPromRuleDTO (e.g. ruler-only labels set before first evaluation) render blank until Prometheus propagates. List rows show missing summaries/labels for freshly-created or freshly-edited rules during the propagation window — a field-fidelity regression versus the review-base implementation that read these from the ruler rule.

[BUG] useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities calls isPluginProvidedRule(rule) and prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) without a null guard, but the hook is invoked with `rule === skipToken ? undefined : rule` from both useGrafanaPromRuleAbility and useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities. Every datasource (cloud/Mimir) rule row in the list view passes skipToken into AlertRuleMenu's useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities, so this hook runs with undefined on every render; if either type guard dereferences the rule (as rulerRuleType.grafana.rule does via rule.grafana_alert), each cloud rule row throws and the entire list view crashes instead of rendering.

[BUG] useAllRulerRuleAbilities hardcodes `const isFederated = false;` with a TODO comment, replacing the previous isFederatedRuleGroup check that made federated rules immutable. Federated Grafana rule groups (the case the deleted check existed for) are now reported as mutable: the Delete/Update/Pause menu items become supported and enabled for federated rules, so a user who deletes one gets a real destructive API call on a rule that the system previously guaranteed was not editable or removable.

[ADVISORY] GrafanaGroupLoader now renders only promResponse rules and deleted the matchRules machinery that surfaced ruler-only rules as 'Creating' and prom-only rules as 'Deleting' RuleOperationListItems. Rules in the ruler→prometheus propagation window silently vanish from the list: a just-created rule is invisible until propagation completes (user thinks creation failed and retries), and a just-deleted rule disappears instantly with no 'Deleting' feedback — while the diff simultaneously removes the logWarning that previously made this divergence observable.

[ADVISORY] getEditableIdentifier returns undefined for any non-Grafana promRule (cloud rules passed promRule-only), and the component then returns null, silently hiding the entire action bar. Any caller of RuleActionsButtons with only a cloud/datasource promRule loses Edit/Delete buttons with no UI feedback beyond a logWarning analytics event; the rule appears to have no actions, and nothing in the render output tells the user or the developer why.

[ADVISORY] The href is built without the createReturnTo() parameter that the deleted GrafanaRuleLoader.tsx version included (createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`, { returnTo })), so the user's list-view filter state is lost on navigation. Users who click a rule from the filtered list view and then press Back/Edit-return land on the unfiltered rule list, silently losing their filter/pagination context on every rule navigation.

adjudication.rationale: In GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx, beforeEach grants global and folder permissions including AlertingRuleUpdate and AlertingRuleDelete (via grantUserPermissions and setFolderAccessControl). In this diff, AlertRuleMenu was changed to also check abilities via useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities for Grafana Prom rules and OR them with ruler abilities, computing canDelete/canPause as true when those permissions exist. Therefore the More-menu is expected to include additional menuitems like Delete (and likely Pause/Restore depending on paused state), making `byRole('menuitem').getAll().length` greater than 4; the test’s `expect(menuItems.length).toBe(4)` is inconsistent with the permissions setup and will fail.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces and exports a bespoke `skipToken` (`export const skipToken = Symbol('ability-skip-token');`) in `useAbilities.ts` and uses it in components (`AlertRuleMenu.tsx`, `RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx`) to “skip” ability evaluation by passing `skipToken` into `useGrafanaPromRuleAbility/Abilities`. This creates a new, local skip convention that is separate from any existing skip-token patterns used elsewhere (not shown in the diff) and could be easy to misuse: the hook only treats *this exact* symbol as the skip case (`rule === skipToken ? undefined : rule`), so passing a different skip token (or any non-rule sentinel) would silently be treated as a rule value and degrade abilities to “false” behavior rather than an explicit skip/error. That’s an architecture/maintainability concern rather than a directly verifiable runtime defect introduced here.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows AlertRuleMenu always calls both `useRulerRuleAbilities(...)` and `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule(promRule) ? promRule : skipToken, ...)` (AlertRuleMenu.tsx). Even when `skipToken` is passed, `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` still invokes `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(rule === skipToken ? undefined : rule)` (useAbilities.ts), which unconditionally runs `useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable` (calling `useFolder(folderUID)`), `useGrafanaRulesSilenceSupport()`, and `useCanSilenceInFolder(rule?.folderUid)`. This is a concrete, diff-grounded performance/architecture concern (extra per-row hook work on list pages), not a functional correctness defect proven by the diff.

A user browsing a list containing a non-Grafana promRule that reaches this component gets a rule row with no actions at all and only a backend analytics warning; the early return conflates 'cannot edit' with 'cannot render any button'.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce an early return in `RuleActionsButtons.V2` when `getEditableIdentifier(...)` cannot build an identifier: `if (!identifier) { return null; }` (new code in `RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx`). `getEditableIdentifier` returns `undefined` when there is no `rule` and `promRule` is not a Grafana prom rule (`prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule(promRule)`), logging only `logWarning('Unable to construct an editable rule identifier')`. This would remove the entire action button row for that rule item. However, the diff does not show a concrete call site that passes a non-Grafana `promRule` without a `rulerRule`; the new primary caller (`GrafanaRuleListItem`) passes a `GrafanaPromRuleDTO`, for which an identifier is constructed. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new GrafanaRuleListItem drops the `returnTo` query parameter that the deleted GrafanaRuleLoader added via createReturnTo(), and drops the `is_paused` fallback from the ruler rule (isPaused: rule?.isPaused with no ruler fallback). adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] summary is now sourced from rule.annotations?.summary (prom payload) instead of the ruler rule's annotations, and the entire item no longer merges ruler-rule data, so fields absent from GrafanaPromRuleDTO (e.g. ruler-only labels set before first evaluation) render blank until Prometheus propagates. adjudication.rationale: The diff removes all Ruler API usage from the Grafana list path (GrafanaGroupLoader no longer queries getGrafanaRulerGroup and no longer merges/matches rulerRule + promRule; GrafanaRuleLoader is deleted). The new GrafanaRuleListItem now renders labels/summary solely from the Prom payload (e.g., `summary={rule.annotations?.summary}` and `labels: labels` from `GrafanaPromRuleDTO`), whereas the previous implementation sourced these from `rulerRule` (`annotations.summary`, `labels = {}` from the ruler DTO) and used Prom only for health/state. This is a concrete behavioral change that can reduce field fidelity if Prom data lags or omits fields that were previously available from the Ruler rule, but the diff alone cannot prove the propagation-lag symptom always occurs, so it’s better classified as a specific edge-case/behavior tradeoff concern rather than a definite bug.

Inside `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`, the memoized computation calls `prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` and `isPluginProvidedRule(rule)` without an explicit `rule` guard, even though `rule` can be `undefined` in this code path (e.g., `AlertRuleMenu` passes `skipToken` when the rule is not a Grafana Prom rule). Whether this actually crashes depends on the implementations/signatures of those helpers (not shown in the diff), so the claimed definite list-view crash is not verifiable from the diff alone, but it is a concrete, diff-grounded robustness concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] useAllRulerRuleAbilities hardcodes `const isFederated = false;` with a TODO comment, replacing the previous isFederatedRuleGroup check that made federated rules immutable. adjudication.rationale: The diff verifiably removes the dual-source matching behavior in `GrafanaGroupLoader.tsx`: it no longer queries the ruler API (`useGetGrafanaRulerGroupQuery` removed), deletes `matchRules`, stops rendering ruler-only rules with `RuleOperation.Creating`, stops rendering prom-only rules with `RuleOperationListItem`/`RuleOperation.Deleting`, and removes the `logWarning` that reported mismatches.
